item.title: 'Tip of the iceberg': NJ illegal voting scandal explodes with more key systems at risk
item.description: Roughly 75,000 noncitizens were summoned for jury duty in New Jersey as GOP lawmakers demand a bipartisan subpoena probe into voter registration.
item.content:encoded:
The top Republican on New Jersey’s Judiciary Committee says she repeatedly warned state officials that automatic voter registration lacked adequate safeguards but was routinely dismissed, as thousands more noncitizens have now been been found on sensitive systems.

Sen. Kristin Corrado, R-Totowa, told Fox News Digital that Gov. Mikie Sherrill's motor voter controversy reinforced Republican demands for a bipartisan investigation with subpoena power, warning the administration's review was too narrowly focused and likely failed to capture the full scope of the problem.

"We didn't just reach out to the Motor Vehicle Commissioner. We reached out to Secretary of State [at the time, Lt. Gov. Taheshia Way]. We were not satisfied with the answers that we got from the motor vehicle commissioner, which I can tell you were basically, ‘we have signs up, they're put on notice… that if you're not a citizen, you can't register to vote’."

"So people were on the honor system. We did not think that was acceptable or satisfactory or enough of a safeguard," she said, adding that the common refrain was of an "honor system."

RNC LEGAL VICTORY CLEARS NORTH CAROLINA VOTER ROLL PURGE OF NONCITIZENS THROUGH JURY RESPONSES

Corrado and others, including Senate Minority Leader Anthony Bucco, are now demanding a bipartisan special-investigation with subpoena power.

Asked if they had heard from Senate President Nicholas Scutari, D-Linden, Corrado said his team indicated they wanted to wait for Gov. Mikie Sherrill’s own internal probe to finish.

"I have concerns about that because this independent investigation is very limited in scope. It is limited to what they're calling the motor vehicle ‘glitch’," she said, warning scrutiny should go far beyond the initial area of discovery.

Shortly after Corrado's spoke to Fox News Digital, reports surfaced that roughly 75,000 noncitizens had been summoned for jury duty through state databases, according to multiple reports, broadening the controversy beyond the Motor Vehicle Commission and prompting additional Republican calls for a wider investigation.

Corrado pointed to her repeated requests over the years for clarity on the security of the voting systems and how she was rebuffed as proof the probe needs to be substantial.

Asked about the demand for a full-scale investigation, Scutari credited what the governor is already doing and said he would hold fire until her probe finishes.

"A healthy democracy depends on the security of our voter registration systems and the stewardship of the individuals entrusted with ensuring our elections are free, fair, and accessible. It also depends on public trust, and Governor Sherrill deserves credit for being transparent about these failures… [and] launch[ing] an independent investigation…," Scutari said in-part, confirming Corrado’s comment he would wait for it to finish.

'SHAME ON YOU': SHERRILL KNEW VOTER-ROLL BOMBSHELL WAS COMING WHEN SHE CALLED TRUMP A LIAR, DOJ OFFICIAL SAYS

Former Gov. Phil Murphy’s spokesman Mahen Gunaratna also told Fox News last week that his boss had "no knowledge" of the issues at the MVC.

"I find that hard to believe, but it's incredibly troubling that the governor did not know what his cabinet members were doing or what was going on right underneath him," Corrado responded.

"All [this] put our election integrity at risk, all questions that have to be answered. And the only way to answer those questions is through a bipartisan, legislative committee."

State Joint Budget Committee ranking member Declan O’Scanlon agreed the scandal validated GOP concerns.

"The fact is that the people in charge for so long said this absolutely was impossible; Republicans were ‘conspiracy theorists’," said O’Scanlon, R-Little Silver.

"There are some folks on the extreme on both sides, but those of us in the middle who have said there are real issues here and they were ignored, and we were accused of being conspiracy theorists, only to find out that we were absolutely right; again."

O’Scanlon said he believed the motor-voter revelations were the "tip of the iceberg," and was hours later proven true, as reports surfaced about the 75,000 noncitizens summoned for jury duty.

"This has the potential to be a real scandal," he warned, agreeing that subpoena-powered hearings are a must.

"We need to get on this quickly because we have elections coming up that are critical, that could be slim margins. And also you want the people of New Jersey to believe in the integrity of their voter rolls and their elections," he said.

"We shouldn't dig this hole any deeper."

Fox News Digital reached out to NJCourts and to Sherrill's office for comment.

Peter McAleer, a spokesman for the state court system, told Fox News Digital the jury system pulls from the MVC as well as taxation and elections department lists, with the taxation department legally being permitted to have noncitizens on its own rolls.

"Prospective jurors are asked about their citizenship and other qualifications when they complete the mandatory juror qualification questionnaire. Prospective jurors must certify that they understand that if they submit a knowingly false answer, they can be subject to punishment for contempt of court," he said. "Approximately 75,000 individuals per year are disqualified from juror service based solely on lack of United States citizenship."

Corrado and Bucco also dropped a bill to eliminate motor-voter and implement voter-ID and regular audits of election data systems.

"New Jerseyans need more than just excuses and finger pointing, they deserve action, and there are commonsense steps we can take right now," said Bucco, R-Morristown.

"Get the MVC out of the voter registration business."

State Sen. Joe Pennacchio, R-Boonton, who recently requested additional scrutiny from Attorney General Todd Blanche himself, told Fox News Digital on Saturday the 75,000 figure is a red-flag that Trenton can’t police itself.

SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER

"The disclosure that 75,000 noncitizens were summoned as potential members of juries screams for a thorough federal investigation," Pennacchio said in a Monday statement.

"The governor has blamed [French software firm] IDEMIA, the Murphy administration and of course President Donald Trump for their ever-increasing numbers," he said, calling Sherrill’s investigatory effort a "whitewash."

"As the scope of this problem grows daily and with the refusal of the Democratic Legislature to investigate, it is obvious the U.S. Attorney General's office must take charge," he said.

item.title: Nancy Guthrie Sheriff Chris Nanos says he's 'still positive' case will be resolved despite long wait
item.description: Pima County Sheriff Chris Nanos says investigators are sorting through massive amounts of DNA and video evidence in the Nancy Guthrie abduction case.
item.content:encoded:
Pima County Sheriff Chris Nanos says he's "still positive" the Nancy Guthrie case will be resolved as investigators continue to dig through evidence more than 25 weeks after her home invasion abduction in Tucson, Arizona.

"We have so much DNA to sort through," Nanos said in an interview aired on "Today."

Guthrie is the 84-year-old mother of one of the show's co-hosts, Savannah Guthrie.

NANCY GUTHRIE'S SUSPECTED ABDUCTION: TIMELINE OF EVENTS IN DISAPPEARANCE OF 'TODAY' HOST'S MOM

"We have so much, in terms of video evidence, to look at," Nanos added. "So I'm still positive that we're here to resolve this case."

The sheriff's remarks came hours after Savannah Guthrie released a new video plea to her mother's abductors on Instagram, urging them to "make the right choice" and tell the family where to look for her.

A federal source told Fox News Monday that Guthrie consulted with law enforcement before releasing the video.

SAVANNAH GUTHRIE'S EMOTIONAL PLEA TO MOM'S KIDNAPPER MAY SIGNAL 'NEW LINE OF COMMUNICATION': REPORT

"It's not clear why Savannah decided to release this message now, but it could be a response to a potential new line of communication," Guthrie's NBC colleague Erin McLaughlin reported Tuesday. "Experts say the language appears to be pointed at whoever committed the crime, though law enforcement have not provided any public updates in the investigation recently."

FOLLOW THE FOX TRUE CRIME TEAM ON X

Recent comments from FBI Director Kash Patel explained the technical process investigators used to recover cached recordings from Guthrie's Nest doorbell camera that were facing imminent deletion in a back-end Google system. But Patel made the video public back on Feb. 10.

SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST TRUE CRIME NEWS

Nanos did not immediately respond to follow-up questions from Fox News Digital. Investigators had scoured the neighborhoods surrounding Guthrie's home and her daughter Annie's house nearby in search of video evidence that might show a suspect or suspect vehicle earlier in the investigation.

GOT A TIP?

"I wonder how many 'leads' they’ve covered," said Jason Pack, a retired FBI supervisory agent who has been closely following the case. "There would be thousands...running down every device on the phone tower and their Wi-Fi router etc."

The case would not be considered cold until all potential leads are exhausted without answers, experts have told Fox News Digital, and Pack said it doesn't appear to have gone cold yet.

LISTEN TO THE NEW 'CRIME & JUSTICE WITH DONNA ROTUNNO' PODCAST

"If the sheriff says they have that much DNA and all of that video, then I don’t think you can call it cold until they’ve rectified those leads one way or the other," he said.

There are likely terabytes worth of digital evidence in the case, he said.

Anyone with information on the case is asked to dial 1-800-CALL-FBI. An anonymous reward can also be obtained by calling 520-88-CRIME with information that leads to an arrest in the case.

"It’s a lot of pressure on criminals to keep such a hard secret, especially something so high profile," Pack added. "You have the pressure from others involved of potentially being killed for talking or ratting them out. And the pressure of the over million-dollar reward on the other side."

Fox News' Matt Finn contributed to this report.

item.title: Anthony Fauci's Hollywood supporters: Julia Roberts, Katy Perry and Orlando Bloom among celebrity backers
item.description: From Julia Roberts' "personal hero" to Katy Perry and Orlando Bloom's "Fauci Gang," Hollywood's biggest stars rallied behind Dr. Anthony Fauci during COVID-19.
item.content:encoded:
Julia Roberts, Katy Perry and Orlando Bloom were among Dr. Anthony Fauci's biggest celebrity supporters during the height of the COVID-19 pandemic.

As the 85-year-old infectious disease expert became the face of America's COVID-19 response after the pandemic became a global crisis in March 2020, he also attracted an unlikely fan club in Hollywood – including Brad Pitt portraying him on "Saturday Night Live at Home." 

While chronicling his management of the spiraling health emergency, Fauci also wrote frequently of his rapidly rising fame in his private 2020 journals, which were released by Senate Homeland Security Committee Chairman Rand Paul, R-Ky, earlier this week.

FAUCI'S NEWLY RELEASED COVID DIARIES REVEAL BIZARRE FIXATION ON FAME AS PANDEMIC DEATHS MOUNTED

"The situation with my national and international fame is explosive and really unimaginable," Fauci wrote in a May 21, 2020 entry in his diary.

"It is not hyoperbole [sic] to say that today I am the most famous and talked about person in the country and one of the most recognizable peson [sic] in the world," he added.

Fauci also dedicated significant space across numerous entries to logging his personal interactions with Hollywood A-listers, including Julia Roberts, Barbra Streisand and Sean Penn among others.

INSIDE FAUCI'S PRIVATE DIARY: WHAT HE WROTE ABOUT TRUMP, TV PERSONALITIES AND CELEBRITIES

As Fauci comes under increasing scrutiny ahead of his scheduled testimony before the Senate Homeland Security Committee as part of its investigation into the origins of the pandemic, here's a look at the celebrities who publicly championed the longtime public health official during the pandemic.

Julia Roberts raved over Fauci while conducting an Instagram Live interview with him as part of ONE Campaign’s new #PassTheMic series.

"How rad that we have maybe the coolest man on the planet right now," the Oscar winner told viewers before Fauci joined her on the video call. "Wow, this is intense."

Roberts then gasped and beamed when Fauci appeared on the screen, saying, "Oh, this is such a thrill."

"This is a thrill for me because there are very few experts of anything in the world, and you truly have emerged as a personal hero for me," she added. "Just to have this little corner of your time for us is such a joy."

In a May 2020 diary entry, Fauci wrote about his "wonderful discussion" with Roberts, who he described as "absolutely fabulous" and "totally down to earth." He also shared that he was "embarrassed" when she told him that he was her personal hero.

On Feb. 10, 2021, Fauci detailed how Roberts presented him with amfAR's Award of Courage virtually from her home in California. "When my image came up on the screen she gasped and said that every time she sees me her throat gets dry and she gets nervous and excused herself to go into the kitchen and get a glass of water," he wrote.

In April 2020, Kim Kardashian organized a private Zoom call with Fauci which included 36 other celebrities, athletes and influencers. Katy Perry, Orlando Bloom, Gwyneth Paltrow, Ashton Kutcher, Mila Kunis, Brad Falchuk, Tiffany Haddish, 2 Chainz and Dennis Quaid were among the notable attendees.

"It was a whole bunch of movie stars and some sports figures and they wanted to know about what they could do to stay safe, about wearing masks and avoiding crowds," Fauci said of the hour-long call in a November 2020 interview with CNN. "I was impressed by the questions they asked, by their level of sophistication."

EXPOSED FAUCI DIARY SHOWS HE ESTIMATED COVID-19 DEATH RATE TO BE MUCH LOWER THAN WHAT HE TOLD CONGRESS

Fauci explained that he agreed to the call due to the group's enormous reach, noting that they had "megaphones" and "could get the word out about staying safe."

"Each of them has enormous numbers of followers on their social media accounts," he told CNN. "I could say to them, for example, it's important to wear a mask, and they get on their accounts and say 'wear a mask' and it goes out to an additional couple of million people."

Katy Perry and Orlando Bloom, who were engaged at the time, actively demonstrated their support for Fauci as the crisis was unfolding. Along with participating in the Zoom call, the former couple donned matching black hoodies emblazoned with the wording "Fauci Gang" for an Instagram post that Bloom shared in May 2020.

"Double tap if you’re in the #drfauci gang," Bloom wrote in the caption.

The hoodies were created as part of a Jerry Media x PizzaSlime collaboration and priced at $69. According to Bustle, the first batch of hoodies quickly sold out after their release. A portion of the proceeds from each sale benefited the CDC Foundation's Coronavirus Emergency Response Fund.

Jennifer Garner publicly praised Fauci before hosting the infectious disease expert for a lengthy Instagram Live in September 2020 in which they discussed parents' concerns during the pandemic.

Garner later shared the interview in an Instagram post, writing in the caption, "Conversation with Dr. Fauci Back-to-School/vaccine/sports/and more questions answered here. I love Dr. Fauci—and you will, too."

The actress and Fauci's conversation spanned a wide range of topics including schools reopening, youth sports, vaccines, vitamins, flu shots and when Americans could safely return to movie theaters.

During the interview, Garner expressed her gratitude to Fauci, telling him, "I just wanted to start by just saying thank you for never lying to us. Thank you for always giving it to us straight."

"I know that you have saved, I mean, countless lives," she added.

TOM HANKS JOKES ABOUT THE NAME HE WOULD GIVE CORONAVIRUS VACCINE

Leonardo DiCaprio honored Fauci during the National Italian American Foundation's 2020 virtual gala, where the infectious disease expert received the Leonardo da Vinci Award for Leadership in Health and Science.

"While COVID is keeping most of us at home, people like Dr. Fauci go to work each morning with one goal: to see our nation through the most devastating pandemic in a century," DiCaprio said via the Washingtonian.

"I am delighted that NIAF is honoring his lifelong commitment to serving the public good, we are fortunate to have Dr Fauci's leadership and guidance in these difficult times," he added.

Other celebrities who shared tributes to Fauci at the gala included Al Pacino, Robert De Niro, Martin Scorsese, Francis Ford Coppola, Michael Douglas, Patti LuPone, Bono, Marisa Tomei, Alan Alda, Dionne Warwick and Angelica Huston.

Matthew McConaughey gave Fauci one of his biggest celebrity platforms during the pandemic when he interviewed the infectious disease expert on Instagram in August 2020.

During their 40-minute conversation, McConaughey and Fauci discussed COVID-19 myths and vaccines. The Oscar winner expressed his anger and disappointment over how he felt the virus had become "politicized."

"Like a lot of people, I've been more than disillusioned — actually quite full of rage — at how COVID has been politicized," McConaughey said.

The actor closed their conversation by embracing Fauci's call for Americans to "pull together" as the former Chief Medical Advisor to the President noted they had done in the aftermath of World War II and 9/11.

"This is equivalent to that, Matthew. We've got to pull together, absolutely," Fauci said.

"That's it," McConaughey said. "We can have our freedom and our party later. Right now, let's pull together."

Alyssa Milano was among Hollywood's most vocal defenders of Fauci during the pandemic. The actress frequently shared his interviews on social media, encouraged followers to trust the nation's top infectious disease expert and repeatedly criticized political attacks against him as debates over masks, shutdowns and vaccines intensified.

However, Milano, who is a longtime critic of President Donald Trump, publicly expressed frustration with Fauci as she shared her opinion that he hadn't been outspoken enough in challenging the administration's response to the pandemic.

"Dr. Fauci might be great and a national treasure, but please let us not forget that he just sat there as Trump made ridiculous uneducated public health claims," she wrote on X in July 2020. "He has also allowed the White House to silence him as things continued to spiral out of control."

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

Mark Ruffalo repeatedly praised Fauci and amplified the infectious disease expert on social media. In an April 2020 post on X, Ruffalo wrote, "Thank you Dr. Fauci for speaking truth to power."

Throughout the pandemic, Ruffalo shared the doctor's public health guidance with his followers, including posting Fauci's interviews along with vaccine information and messages encouraging Americans to follow scientific recommendations.

As criticism of Fauci intensified in mid-2020, Ruffalo often defended the infectious disease expert on social media. He amplified stories defending Fauci and called attention to what he viewed as attacks on public health experts.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER

George Takei was one of Fauci's most consistent celebrity supporters on social media. The "Star Trek" actor celebrated former President Joe Biden's decision to keep Fauci as chief medical adviser when he took office in January 2021.

In an X post he shared in December 2020, Takei shared a clip about Fauci continuing his role in Biden's administration, writing, "Wonderful news, indeed."

Throughout 2020 and beyond, Takei used his large social media following to defend Fauci, praise his work and criticize attacks on him.

item.title: China, Russia, Iran and North Korea form 'axis of aggressors' that could overwhelm US, book warns
item.description: A new report documents 616 instances of security cooperation among China, Russia, Iran and North Korea, warning of a dangerous simultaneity problem.
item.content:encoded:
China, Russia, Iran and North Korea are acting as a strategically aligned bloc even without a formal mutual-defense treaty, according to a new Foundation for Defense of Democracies book warning that their cooperation could leave the United States confronting multiple crises simultaneously.

The book, "Axis of Aggressors: Countering the Cooperation of China, Russia, Iran and North Korea," examines how the four authoritarian governments support one another across military, economic, cyber and technology domains.

Its authors acknowledge that the grouping is not a NATO-style alliance. It has no unified command, comprehensive defense commitment or complete trust among its members. But they argue that its practical effects are already visible in active conflicts.

TRUMP TO CONFRONT XI AT HIGH-STAKES SUMMIT OVER CHINA BACKING FOR IRAN, RUSSIA

"I just got back from a couple of weeks in Ukraine, and when I’m sitting in Ukraine, it’s really obvious to me that Ukraine is fighting Russia, North Korea, Iran and China," retired Rear Adm. Mark Montgomery, one of the book’s three authors, told Fox News Digital.

Montgomery pointed to North Korean ammunition and troops, Iranian drones and production expertise, and Chinese economic and technological support for Moscow.

"China is backstopping the whole thing, providing the economic backstop to Russia’s economy so they can survive this four-year catastrophic event for Russia," Montgomery said. "They’re providing microelectronics that we see in ballistic, cruise and hypersonic missiles."

The book’s researchers documented 616 instances of security cooperation among the four governments from Jan. 1, 2019, through Dec. 31, 2025, including arms transfers, weapons development, military exercises, intelligence sharing and military exchanges.

The central danger, Montgomery said, is what the book calls the "simultaneity problem."

"We don’t get to handle these with a singularity anymore. We have to handle this with a simultaneity," he said. "And I don’t think we can handle two problems at once, much less three or four."

During a potential confrontation between China and Taiwan, Montgomery said, North Korea could threaten South Korea or conduct limited attacks intended to pin down U.S. forces. A conflict involving Russia and NATO’s Baltic members could be accompanied by Iranian terrorism or other hostile activity.

THREE KEY REASONS WHY AMERICA CANNOT AFFORD TO LOSE TAIWAN TO COMMUNIST CHINA

The book identifies China-Russia military cooperation as the axis’s most consequential bilateral relationship. Chinese dual-use products have helped sustain Russia’s defense industrial base, while Moscow is transferring technology and battlefield lessons that could assist China in a Pacific conflict.

North Korea has supplied Russia with millions of artillery rounds, ballistic missiles and troops, while Moscow has assisted Pyongyang’s missile, space, drone and nuclear programs, according to the book.

Iran has provided Russia with drones and production knowledge. The book warns that Russian and Chinese assistance could also help Tehran rebuild military capabilities damaged during its conflicts with Israel and the United States.

"The longer they can entangle the United States, whether it was in Ukraine or in Iran, China and Russia are the primary beneficiaries," Montgomery said.

Economic ties underpin the military cooperation, according to co-author Elaine Dezenski, who described the four-country economy as a "fractured alignment."

"These four players are bound together more by necessity than they are by a specific trust or shared strategy among them," Dezenski told Fox News Digital. "China needs energy. Russia and Iran need buyers for their oil and gas. And North Korea needs any lifeline that it can get."

China purchases discounted Russian and Iranian energy while providing goods, technology and access to its domestic market.

The relationships remain unequal. Russia and Iran compete to sell similar products, while China can seek other suppliers. But Dezenski said those divisions should not obscure the benefits the cooperation provides.

"The economics of this very much underpin the foundations for the military engagement that we see," she said.

The book says China purchases as much as 95% of Iran’s oil exports. Some sanctioned oil is routed through third countries, relabeled or processed by independent Chinese refineries known as "teapots."

"The export juggernaut that is China today is fueled by sanctioned oil and gas," Dezenski said.

TRUMP MAY CLAIM HE WON THE FIGHT WITH IRAN, BUT THERE’S A BIGGER WAR ALREADY UNDERWAY

Dezenski also warned that China, Russia and Iran are developing payment systems outside traditional Western banking infrastructure. More trade is being settled in yuan through China’s Cross-Border Interbank Payment System, or CIPS, potentially reducing Washington’s ability to enforce sanctions through the dollar system.

"We need to really think about that sooner rather than later, before this alternative payment system becomes too big to tackle," Dezenski said.

Montgomery said the line between criminal hackers and government operatives is often deliberately blurred in all four countries.

"These regimes routinely outsource work to criminal groups to keep their own hands clean, and those groups are increasingly networking with each other," he said.

The book cites ties involving Iranian cybercriminals and Russian ransomware groups, Chinese actors on Russian dark-web forums, and Russian and North Korean state-backed hackers using shared operational infrastructure.

Carrie Filipetti, executive director of the Vandenberg Coalition and a former State Department official during the first Trump administration, said drone warfare demonstrates how assistance moves among the countries.

"Chinese components are used to create Iranian drones, which are then deployed by the Russians against Ukrainian civilians," Filipetti told Fox News Digital.

She said the relationship has also endangered American troops, pointing to the January 2024 Tower 22 attack in Jordan, which killed three U.S. Army Reserve soldiers and wounded more than 40 service members.

"The military and ideological relationship between Russia and Iran is not just a theoretical threat to the United States — American service members have been killed as a result of it," Filipetti said.

Filipetti said the attack used an Iranian drone and Russian tactics developed during the war in Ukraine. "These adversaries don’t agree on everything, but they do on one thing: to reorient the world away from America and the West," she said. "Our service members and citizens will continue to suffer until we treat the threat as the united threat it is."

Retired Air Force Lt. Gen. Richard Newton said the danger stems not only from military modernization in each country, but from the degree to which the four governments are increasingly coordinating.

"I couldn’t agree more with the underlying findings the authors present regarding the rapid military modernization unfolding across multiple domains — air, sea, land, space and cyber — emanating from China, Russia, Iran and North Korea," Newton told Fox News Digital.

"These nation-states represent extraordinary adversarial challenges for the United States. That’s concerning enough," he said. "But a major challenge President Trump is facing in his second administration is the level and degree of integration, synchronization and coordination among these four adversaries, who are more unified today than ever in their collective pursuits to threaten U.S. national security interests."

Newton said the changing character of warfare, demonstrated by more than four years of fighting between Russia and Ukraine and the current U.S.-Iran conflict, has compounded the threat.

"Couple that with the changing nature of warfare we’ve been witnessing," he said, "and the task to defend our nation is now much more complex and daunting."

Retired Air Force Gen. Philip Breedlove, who served as NATO supreme allied commander and commander of U.S. European Command from 2013 to 2016, argued that Washington’s language understates the severity of the confrontation.

"We often say that we are in ‘strategic competition’ with China and Russia. They are at war with us," Breedlove told Fox News Digital.

Breedlove said China, Russia, Iran and North Korea "are not partners looking for cooperation with the U.S.," but governments seeking to "diminish and defeat" American power.

"The enemy gets a vote," Breedlove said. "Our enemies are voting by their support to Russia and Iran."

He added that assistance from the other countries has become increasingly important to Moscow as it struggles to sustain its war.

"Aid is critical to Russia," Breedlove said. "Russia is failing and becoming ever more dependent on its allies."

The authors recommend stronger coordination with allies, expanded defense production, greater protection of U.S. critical infrastructure and more aggressive sanctions enforcement.

Dezenski called for targeting the full network supporting sanctioned Russian and Iranian oil, including refineries, ports, insurers and financiers, rather than focusing primarily on individual vessels.

"We need to treat this axis as a threat, as a combined threat," Montgomery said, "that will confront us in every one of our crisis areas."

item.title: Chicken wing prices are down — here's why your favorite restaurant may not cut prices
item.description: Wholesale chicken wing prices plunged 66% from pandemic-era highs, and restaurants are passing savings to customers with specials ahead of football season.
item.content:encoded:
It's National Chicken Wing Day, and fans of one of America's most iconic foods have reason to celebrate: Wing prices have fallen after years of soaring costs.

Wholesale whole wing prices are down from a year ago. There's also a steady supply available, according to a July market trend report published by Performance Foodservice.

It's likely chicken wing lovers will be able to take advantage of those lower wholesale costs through deals and specials at restaurants, Kipper Greist, managing partner of Jumby Bay Island Grill in Jupiter, Florida, told Fox News Digital.

BONELES WINGS ARE STILL WINGS, JUDGE RULES, AND CHEFS TAKE A BITE OF THE BATTLE

"Prices fluctuate constantly on every menu item," Greist said. "If one item drops, three go up. The cost of reprinting menus is thousands of dollars, so it isn't cost-effective to raise or lower prices when the market changes. We would rather offer specials like our 99-cent wings on Wednesdays and during football season."

The lower prices come as chicken production has outpaced expectations, helping keep wing supplies strong and wholesale costs in check.

The dip in cost was due to U.S. meat-chicken producers "boosting domestic production by 2.2% in 2025, aided by lower feed costs," Wells Fargo reported.

"Chicken production, including wings, of course, is running ahead of earlier expectations as hatchability and liveability have somewhat surprisingly improved," Tom Super, senior vice president of public affairs for the National Chicken Council (NCC), told Fox News Digital. "That is, the poultry genetists and live-production management have apparently begun to overcome these two challenges."

Wholesale wing prices have strengthened this week, according to the U.S. Department of Agriculture, but they remain a bargain for restaurants and grocery retailers, Super said.

"With the wing supply somewhat fixed, fluctuating consumer demand heavily influences the ups and downs in wholesale prices," Super said.

Wholesale wing prices opened in 2025 below $1.00 per pound and rose only modestly to slightly above $1.10 per pound — a 66% decline from their historic pandemic-era high above $3.20 per pound, according to Southern Ag Today.

"When wing prices rise to unattractive levels for food service buyers, they tend to pull back on wing promotions and special price offerings," Super said. 

"Then, as wing prices move to much more affordable levels, food service buyers, especially those dedicated to wings, jump back into marketing wings more aggressively."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS

Chicken wings are also "an affordable protein option," according to the NCC. 

"Consumers are continuing to value and appreciate wholesome protein in their foods," Super said. 

This trend, combined with favorable pricing, offers chicken wing lovers the opportunity to gather with friends and family affordably, he added.

"If there is one menu item that never grows old, it's the chicken wing," Greist said. "Its versatility attracts every genre. It can be an appetizer for a group or a meal for others."

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

Every wing lover is different, Greist said.

"Some like a large, meaty wing, while others prefer the smaller wings," he said. "The sauce is where it's at! Customers are trending away from traditional sauces and experimenting more with hot garlic, garlic Parmesan, Thai chili and mango barbecue."

The origin story of America's love affair with the chicken wing varies, but a widely accepted version credits the Anchor Bar in Buffalo, New York, with popularizing one of the least-desirable parts of the chicken by deep-frying the wings, coating them in hot butter sauce and serving them with blue-cheese dressing and celery.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

"With new flavors, spices and rubs constantly offering another great reason to try wings again, wing lovers and want-to-be wing lovers find the next wonderful taste an attraction hard to resist," Super said.

item.title: EXCLUSIVE: New America 250 monument lets families find military relatives in seconds: 'I had tears in my eyes'
item.description: Visitors search loved ones' names and watch them appear on towering digital flags at the Lincoln Memorial as part of the America250 celebration.
item.content:encoded:
WASHINGTON — Millions of Americans celebrating the nation's 250th birthday are now able to search for parents, grandparents, siblings and loved ones who served in the U.S. military—and watch their names appear seconds later across two towering digital American flags on the steps of the Lincoln Memorial.

After opening Monday as one of the signature installations of the nationwide America250 celebration, the National Military Monument sponsored by USAA honors more than 41 million Americans whose military service spans from the Revolutionary War through today.

Built from military records, public databases, veterans organizations and voluntary submissions, the interactive installation invites visitors to discover their own family's place in American history rather than simply observe it. Fox News Digital received an exclusive preview ahead of the public opening.

EVERYDAY REVOLUTIONARY WAR HEROES TAKE CENTER STAGE IN TRUMP'S 'SPIRIT OF '76' EXHIBIT

Unlike many of Washington's memorials, which commemorate presidents, battles or individual wars, organizers say the National Military Monument was designed to recognize the millions of Americans whose names rarely appear in history books but whose service helped shape the country over the last 250 years.

Visitors begin not by reading a plaque, but by pulling out their smartphones.

After scanning a QR code at one of several kiosks, visitors receive a six-digit code that summons a loved one's name onto one of two towering digital American flags overlooking the Reflecting Pool. Each side of the monument cycles through roughly 1,500 names every 45 seconds, or about 480,000 names every hour.

WHITE HOUSE CONDEMNS 'TARGETED SABOTAGE' OF REFLECTING POOL AS REPAIRS PUSHED PAST JULY 4 CELEBRATION

Standing on the Lincoln Memorial Plaza between the Lincoln Memorial and the Washington Monument, the installation was placed there because organizers wanted one of the National Mall's most heavily visited locations during the America250 celebration.

Families gathered around kiosks searching for relatives. Veterans waited quietly as names appeared overhead. At one point, George Washington's name stretched across the display, a visual reminder that the monument traces military service all the way from Lexington and Concord to Afghanistan and beyond.

The monument combines military records and public databases dating back to the Revolutionary War along with information from veterans service organizations and USAA members who chose to participate. Because no single government archive contains every American who has served, organizers say the project will continue growing as veterans and families verify military service and submit names not yet represented. Some currently serving military members and veterans may not appear because of privacy protections or gaps in historical records.

GOLD STAR WIDOW SAYS 'BLESSINGS ARE INFINITE' AFTER STRANGERS FLOOD HUSBAND'S ARLINGTON GRAVE

For Navy veteran and USAA Creative Director John Guzman, the monument's purpose became clear with one search.

Standing beside one of the kiosks during Fox News Digital's preview, Guzman entered the name of his grandfather, Walter Allen, who served during World War II.

"There he is," Guzman said as his grandfather's name appeared across the monument.

Even though he knew what would happen, the moment caught him off guard.

"Even though I knew I was going to find him, it's still heavy to see it come up in all of the best ways," he said.

"This is one of the role models I had growing up from a very, very young child. And even though he's not with us now, the whole family would be incredibly proud to see him here."

Asked what his grandfather would think, Guzman smiled.

"I know him well enough to know he would say there's about 100 other guys he'd rather see up there... I can hear his voice right now saying that."

The same experience played out for first-time visitors Tim and Tenika Eardley, who traveled from Wyoming expecting to see Washington's historic landmarks—not the newest one.

The couple searched for a family member currently serving in the National Guard.

"My uncle and her brother—we looked him up on there," their son, Warren Eardley said. "That was really neat just to be able to see him on there."

For Tenika, the experience transformed the monument from a tourist attraction into something personal.

"It feels really meaningful to be able to know that I can look up any relative or friend or anything like that and be able find them and honor them," she said.

"It feels like such a personalized experience that we really can see those people that we know and love honored right here in D.C."

Bob Labrutta, a retired Air Force major general who now serves as USAA's vice president of survivorship, said that reaction is exactly what organizers hoped visitors would experience.

After nearly four decades in uniform, Labrutta said he thought he understood what the monument represented until he searched for members of his own family.

"I've got two brothers that served," he said. "But when I brought my dad's name up on the side of the wall and I saw him commemorated... I had tears in my eyes and my heart filled with pure joy and pride. Pride in this country. Pride in USAA for doing this."

"Because this is what we should be doing each and every day: honoring, thanking and paying tribute to the military members who have served this nation so nobly."

Labrutta said the installation was intentionally designed to honor not only decorated military leaders but the millions of Americans whose service often goes unrecognized.

"I wouldn't say our soldiers are ordinary," he said. "Our soldiers, sailors, airmen, Marines, Coast Guard members, our Guardians—none of them are ordinary."

"When they raise their right hand, they say not only, 'Send me,' but 'I'm willing to give up my life for this great country.' That makes them extraordinary."

While the monument was created during the nation's semiquincentennial celebration, Labrutta said its purpose extends beyond America's 250th birthday.

"It doesn't just apply to military families," he said. "It applies to all American citizens."

"We wouldn't have had an Independence Day if we wouldn't have had citizens that raised their hand and said, 'You know what? This is worth fighting for.'"

Generation after generation, he said, Americans have protected the freedoms the country enjoys today.

"This is not only for our veterans and for their families," Labrutta said. "This is for all Americans to embrace and to honor."

item.title: NASA at 68: America must lead on the Moon, Mars and beyond—or China will
item.description: Two House committee members argue the U.S. must dominate space exploration as China invests heavily in lunar and satellite network technologies.
item.content:encoded:
On July 29, America will celebrate the birth of the agency that transformed the impossible into the inevitable. For 68 years, the National Aeronautics and Space Administration has led the world in space exploration.

From the Mercury missions to Apollo and the space shuttle program to Artemis, NASA has always represented something larger than rockets and astronauts. It is a reminder that when America leads with courage, innovation and purpose, the world follows.

Today, that leadership is being tested once again.

NASA CHIEF DECLARES AMERICA 'ABSOLUTELY BACK' IN SPACE RACE, SAYS US WILL BEAT CHINA TO THE MOON

A new space race is underway, and China has made no secret of its ambitions. Beijing is investing heavily in lunar exploration, advanced satellite networks and space technologies with both civilian and military applications. The nation that establishes the rules, infrastructure and presence in space will shape the economic and security landscape for decades to come.

The United States cannot afford to watch from the sidelines.

That’s why we are proud to serve on the House Committee on Science, Space and Technology. Earlier this year, our committee advanced the NASA Reauthorization Act of 2026. This legislation reaffirms our nation’s commitment to human space exploration and authorizes funding for both Artemis and the Moon to Mars program. It also focuses on building a skilled technical workforce to ensure the next generation is ready to take on the mantle of space exploration.

TRUMP SWINGS FOR MOON WITH NUCLEAR REACTOR PLANS AS CHINA, RUSSIA TEAM UP IN SPACE RACE

For years, the United States’ space program languished, underfunded and underappreciated. Today, things have changed. This administration knows how important the space race is to American innovation. The Moon is critical as a testing ground for Mars and deep-space missions. A sustained presence on the Moon could also create opportunities for asteroid mining, providing resources needed for emerging technologies such as quantum computing. This isn’t just about commercial opportunity; it is also critical for national security.

For example, satellites provide critical telecommunications capabilities that allow U.S. forces to communicate securely across the globe in real time. From GPS technology to space-based sensor systems, satellites are integral to military operations. Protecting our space infrastructure isn’t optional. The space race cannot be neck and neck; the United States must dominate.

AS AMERICA MARKS 250 YEARS, OUR GREATEST CHAPTERS ARE STILL AHEAD OF US

History teaches us that American leadership has never been guaranteed. It has been earned through bold investment, scientific excellence and an unwavering belief that tomorrow belongs to those willing to build it. That same spirit carried Neil Armstrong onto the Moon and inspired generations of engineers, scientists, entrepreneurs and service members to push the boundaries of what was possible.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION

As we approach NASA’s birthday, we should celebrate not only our extraordinary achievements but also our responsibility to lead the next chapter. Space is no longer simply the final frontier. It is the next frontier for national security, economic growth, technological innovation and American influence.

The challenge before us is clear. We can either lead the future or allow others to define it for us.

For nearly seven decades, NASA has embodied the American spirit: curiosity, determination and the courage to venture where no one has gone before. As a new generation looks toward the Moon, Mars and beyond, let us ensure the stars continue to shine brightest for a nation that has never been afraid to reach for them.

Republican Mike Haridopolos represents Florida's Eighth Congressional District in the United States House of Representatives.

item.title: No Jews on Mamdani’s 'truly representative' NYC judiciary panel, sparking backlash
item.description: Four Jewish bar associations demand Zohran Mamdani correct the exclusion of Jewish members from his 19-person judiciary advisory panel in New York City.
item.content:encoded:
City Hall repeatedly touted New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani’s 19-member judiciary advisory panel as a "truly representative cross-section" of New York City’s legal profession — but four Jewish bar associations say not one Jewish member was appointed.

The groups, backed by the Anti-Defamation League (ADL), are demanding Mamdani correct what they called a profound omission from the influential committee, which screens and recommends candidates for judgeships across the five boroughs and across various different courts, including Criminal Court, Family Court and, on an interim basis, Civil Court.

City Hall touted Mamdani’s 19-member judiciary advisory panel as a "truly representative cross-section" when it was announced July 22. Meanwhile, Mamdani’s own Jan. 2 executive order establishing the committee stated that its membership "shall reflect the cosmopolitan population of the City of New York."

"The members announced today offer a truly representative cross-section of the legal profession in New York City, bringing a wide range of professional experience from all five boroughs to the Mayor’s Advisory Committee on the Judiciary," said Ramzi Kassem, Chief Counsel to the Mayor and City Hall, who supervises the activities of the Committee. 

BLUE STATE MOCKED AFTER 'SEX AND THE CITY' ACTRESS TAPPED TO RECOMMEND TOP JUDGES

"Under Mayor Mamdani’s leadership, [Mayor’s Advisory Committee on the Judiciary] will reach across the legal community to build a broad and highly qualified pool of judicial applicants," Kassem continued. "An independent and impartial judiciary composed of jurists who have served their fellow New Yorkers in a range of legal circumstances is essential to a healthy democracy, and these appointments reflect our administration’s commitment to a fair, inclusive and transparent judicial selection process."

But the Brandeis Association, Jewish Lawyers Guild, Brooklyn Brandeis Society and Queens Brandeis Association — along with other critics — say the absence of even one Jewish member from the 19-person panel exposes a glaring contradiction between City Hall’s rhetoric and its appointments. 

"At a time when antisemitism is rising and Jewish communities are increasingly under threat, excluding Jewish voices from this influential body is not only disheartening, it is dangerous," the groups wrote in a joint letter they sent to Mamdani on Monday. "The absence of Jewish representation on a committee entrusted with shaping the future of our judiciary sends a deeply troubling message to the Jewish community and undermines the committee’s credibility and ability to serve all New Yorkers fairly."

NY ASSEMBLYMAN CALLS FOR DOJ TO INVESTIGATE MAMDANI, PROTECT JEWISH NEW YORKERS AFTER STABBING ATTACKS

In addition to Mamdani, the four groups sent the letter to New York Gov. Kathy Hochul, New York Attorney General Letitia James and New York Chief Judge Rowan Wilson, along with other state, city and judicial officials.

The letter's warning, which included calls to "correct this exclusion," came amid renewed fears over Jewish safety in the city.

On Tuesday, a hammer-carrying intruder entered the grounds of the Jewish Institute of Queens and shoved an 8-year-old boy into a fence during a struggle with security, leaving the child with a head injury, authorities said. Police did not believe the boy was the intended target, and investigators have not established a motive.

The frightening episode followed last week’s alleged hate-crime attack on an Orthodox Jewish man who was stabbed in the chest with a screwdriver shortly after leaving an Upper West Side synagogue. Prosecutors say the suspect shouted "Justice for Islam" and "Allahu Akbar" before committing the attack.

SUSPECT ARRESTED AFTER ALLEGEDLY YELLING ‘ALLAHU AKBAR,' STABBING 2 MEN IN NYC ATTACK

The mayor’s office, the Mayor’s Advisory Committee on the Judiciary and committee Chairman Ali Najmi did not respond to Fox News Digital’s request for comment by publication time. However, Mamdani press secretary Joe Calvello told NBC New York that any suggestion the appointments to the Mayor’s Advisory Committee on the Judiciary were motivated by religion was "false."

Calvello said Mamdani had appointed "a dozen qualified judges from a range of backgrounds, including Jewish judges," and said the administration declined to appoint retired Justice John Leventhal, who is Jewish, after learning he had served on Ghislaine Maxwell’s legal team.

"Make no mistake, the leader of the Democrat Party, Mayor Mamdani, is working to bulldoze the rest of New York government to fit his ideology," Mark Bednar, a principal at Monument Advocacy who previously led communications for former House Speaker Kevin McCarthy and served as communications director for then-Rep. Sean Duffy, told Fox News Digital. "Americans of all backgrounds should take notice of the threat his ideology poses, and to sound the alarm about anyone he appoints to important positions."

Jewish civil rights attorney Gerard Filitti argued that the absence of Jewish members was particularly glaring in a city with the largest Jewish population in the country. He also pointed out the committee’s influence over the courts that hear hate-crime cases.

"His own chief counsel called the slate a truly representative cross-section of the city's legal profession, in the city with the largest Jewish population in America, on the panel that will pick the judges who hear hate-crime cases," Filitti wrote on X. "City Hall did not deny the exclusion. It changed the subject to judges Mamdani appointed elsewhere. Jewish New Yorkers are owed the same representation as everyone else, and this mayor just seated a panel that gives them none."

item.title: Dating's new red flag: Voting the 'wrong' way could leave you single for good
item.description: A psychotherapist explains why dating app bios on Hinge and Bumble now read like political loyalty oaths and why that's destroying real connection.
item.content:encoded:
Somewhere along the way, "swipe right if you're 5 feet 10 inches or taller" turned into "swipe left if you didn't vote the way I wanted." I don't know exactly when the dating profile became a place to list your positions on foreign policy, but if you've opened Hinge or Bumble in any major city lately, you already know what I'm talking about.

Scroll through profiles in New York, D.C. or L.A., and you'll see it instantly. And it's not just one side of the dating pool. Before she tells you her job or what she's looking for, she's told you her pronouns, there's a Palestinian flag next to "no fascists," and somewhere in there, usually bolded, is some version of "if you voted for Trump, don't bother."

The guys aren't any different. Feminist ally bios, "will not date a Republican," a picture holding a sign from the last protest he went to, the same pronoun-in-bio energy, just with a beard. Walk through 20 profiles in a blue city, male or female, and count how many treat their politics like a personality.

AI IS CHANGING MODERN DATING, BUT EXPERTS WARN IT'S MAKING PEOPLE 'RELATIONALLY STUPID'

I'm a psychotherapist, and I've spent close to two decades listening to people talk about their relationships, what's working, what isn't and why they picked who they picked. And I can tell you: None of this is about values. It's about performance. A sign that says "no MAGA" isn't screening for character. It's screening for an audience.

Here's what's actually funny about it: A recent SSRS survey found that more than half of Democrats who use dating apps say sharing political beliefs is very important when picking a match. For Republicans and independents, it's about a quarter. So, one side has turned swiping into a loyalty oath, and the other side is just trying to find someone who'll text back.

I once had a client, a smart, funny woman in her early 30s, who came in to see me and was furious because a guy she'd matched with turned out to be "conservative-adjacent." Not a MAGA hat guy. Not someone spouting anything extreme. He just hadn't put a pronoun in his bio and once mentioned he leaned right on taxes. She was done. Not because he was rude, dishonest, or unkind — none of which she knew yet — but because he failed a purity test before they'd had a single real conversation.

GROWING TREND OF HATING MEN BACKFIRES AS ANTI-MARRIAGE CULTURE LEAVES SINGLE WOMEN LOSING OUT

I've had male clients do the exact same thing in reverse, writing off a woman the second she mentioned she went to church or wasn't "political" enough. Different behavior, same instinct.

Meanwhile, I've watched couples who agree on every political issue under the sun sit across from each other, miserable, because agreeing on Gaza or student loan forgiveness did absolutely nothing to improve how they treat each other when the dishes aren't done or someone forgets an anniversary.

That's the part nobody wants to hear. A shared hatred of the other political tribe is not a foundation for marriage. It's not even a good opening line. It's a filter that screens out perfectly decent people over a bumper sticker while doing nothing to screen out the actual things that end relationships: lying, contempt, cheating and an inability to apologize.

But try telling that to a dating app bio that reads like a DNC press release with a profile photo attached.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION

At some point, "science is real" and "trans rights are human rights" stopped being political statements and became social passwords, a way of announcing which group you belong to before anyone's even said hello. It's less about believing something and more about being seen believing it. And it's turned dating, which used to be awkward but at least honest, into an audition for the right kind of politics.

Maybe the healthiest thing a single person could do right now is delete every political slogan from their profile and see who's left standing. My guess: There are still plenty of people, just fewer performing for an audience that was never going to be a good match for them anyway.

item.title: The next American boom could be here — unless Washington regulates it to death
item.description: A new study called "Boomsday Not Doomsday" argues AI will lower prices on food, housing, and healthcare while creating new jobs across the economy.
item.content:encoded:
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei predicts a white-collar "bloodbath." Senator Bernie Sanders warns AI could wipe out 100 million American jobs. Elon Musk says work may become optional.

The message is everywhere: machines are coming for your paycheck.

That panic is understandable. But wrong. Yes, AI will disrupt and eventually replace some tasks, just as electricity, the farm tractor, and the internet caused the displacement of mundane and, in some cases, miserable jobs like working in hot, sweaty factories or backbreaking work lifting heavy equipment. Yes, some workers will need help adjusting and retraining to the robotics revolution. Yet the fear of mass technological unemployment repeats a mistake doomsayers have made for centuries, from the tractor to the personal computer.

CHRISTIAN UNIVERSITY AIMS TO PRODUCE 'IRREPLACEABLE' GRADUATES AS AI RESHAPES HIGHER EDUCATION

In our new study, "Boomsday Not Doomsday," we show AI can become the most powerful engine of American prosperity in decades. How? AI lowers the price and speeds up production of nearly everything we use: from food, to steel, to cars, to information, to new homes, to new cures for diseases. How does a four day workweek sound?

For most of history, practical expertise was expensive and hard to find. Families, workers and small businesses had to pay consultants, lawyers, programmers, or other specialists, or go without. AI gives Americans useful, personalized assistance for less than the price of a daily cup of coffee, and often for free.

A small-business owner can get help writing a marketing plan. A patient can leave the doctor with clearer instructions. A homeowner can learn whether that crack in the wall requires a professional. A teacher can build custom lesson plans. New health scans can locate possible cancer cells early and save millions of lives.

AI isn’t replacing Americans, it’s making us more capable. It will make life on earth better — especially for the lower half in income, who soon thanks to these productivity improvements have a quality of life that rivals the richest royalty of yesteryear.

The early numbers show how quickly this is happening. Generative AI is growing three times faster than mobile apps or the internet did. Nearly nine in ten organizations now use AI in at least one business function. Americans already value AI tools at $172 billion a year, based on what they’d need to be paid to give them up. Worried about the rising cost of food, gas, housing and health care? Get ready for these things falling in price dramatically.

Widespread prosperity begins like this, with millions of people saving time and money, learning faster and getting more done.

CHINA IS BUILDING AN AI WAR MACHINE. WASHINGTON MUST WAKE UP BEFORE IT’S TOO LATE

We have been through panics before. In 1900, more than one in three Americans worked in agriculture. Today fewer than 2% do and we produce 10 times more food on one-third as much farmland. America did not collapse into permanent unemployment. We grew more food with fewer hands. The economy created hundreds of millions of jobs no one could have imagined. The pattern repeats with every leap forward. Technology automates drudgery, raises productivity, and creates new opportunities.

The numbers agree. Unemployment sits at a low 4.3%. Between 2022 and early 2025, the most AI-exposed workers saw smaller unemployment increases than the least exposed. And demand for AI skills is exploding: job postings seeking them jumped 111% in a single year.

Some young workers feel pressure. The answer, as in every transition, is to help American workers use these tools. When they do, everyday improvements will add up to a richer, healthier, happier country. Prisons and reform schools are using AI to train young people for jobs that are waiting for them.

In medicine, Mayo Clinic has used AI to identify pancreatic cancer up to three years earlier. Physicians at The Permanente Group using AI-note takers save roughly an hour a day. Patients get better care that feels less like an assembly line and more like time with someone who listens.

On Main Street, AI helps workers turn know-how into ownership. Jason Walls, a Kentucky master electrician, watched contractors push EV owners into unneeded and expensive electrical panel upgrades. With no coding background, he used AI to build a website that runs the calculations, generates the reports, and saves families money.

We’re seeing this pattern across the economy, in education, construction, and manufacturing.

No one should pretend that every transition will be painless. But while doomsayers worry that AI moves too fast, the real danger is that America moves too slowly. China would love to swoop in and take our place.

We invented this technology, yet too few of us put it to work. More than half of American adults have tried generative AI, but only 28.3% use it regularly, which leaves the United States 24th out of the 30 countries measured. France and the United Kingdom rank higher.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION

The Chinese get it. Three out of four people there expect AI to improve their economy. They deploy fast: in 2024, China installed 295,045 industrial robots to America’s 34,164. China has some of the most capable and most popular open-source AI models.

Meanwhile, we are all too often hobbling ourselves here at home. State legislatures introduced more than 1,700 AI bills this year. Some Democrats have demanded government ownership of major AI companies while proposing to ban new AI supercomputers.

Washington faces a clear choice. It can tax, regulate, ration, or nationalize this technology, reserving its benefits for itself and the biggest companies — and the Chinese. Or, as we did so effectively with the Internet Revolution, we can lead the world and enjoy the fruits of winning the race.

From the days of Ben Franklin, Thomas Edison, and Henry Ford, America has always led by inventing. Let’s be the leaders, not the laggards. To the victors go the spoils — and for the sake of our economic and national security, the victor MUST be the USA.

Neil Chilson is Head of AI Policy at the Abundance Institute and former chief technologist at the Federal Trade Commission.

item.title: Battle to replace late House Dem goes to overtime after daughter failed to clinch seat
item.description: Marcye Scott and Everton Blair advance to an Aug. 25 runoff election in Georgia's 13th congressional district to fill the late David Scott's seat.
item.content:encoded:
Two Democratic candidates locked in a race to fill the seat left by the late Rep. David Scott, D-Ga., advanced to a runoff election on Tuesday evening after failing to capture 51% of the vote.

The winner of the election will add another Democratic seat in a narrowly divided House of Representatives where Republicans hold 218 seats and Democrats control 212. Adding even one more Democratic member puts increased pressure on Republicans to remain united on party-line legislation.

Marcye Scott, the daughter of the late David Scott, and Everton Blair, chair of the Gwinnett County School Board, will face off against each other in a runoff to represent the Peach State’s 13th Congressional District on Aug. 25.

DAUGHTER OF LATE HOUSE DEM FORCED INTO RUNOFF AFTER FALLING SHORT IN SPECIAL ELECTION

A third candidate, Caesar Gonzales, a Republican, did not advance, receiving only 8.7% of the vote.

Georgia’s 13th Congressional District House seat became open when David Scott, 80, died in office back in April. His office did not disclose a cause of death.

Shortly after his death, Marcye Scott announced her candidacy to fill his seat, pitching herself as the best candidate to continue her father’s legacy.

DEMOCRAT REP DAVID SCOTT DEAD AT 80

"That would be what I definitely want to do, to make sure that his voters, his constituents, do not miss out on what he was offering," Scott said.

Scott has made roads and infrastructure, public safety and transportation key priorities of her campaign, highlighting constituent outreach work she did for her father.

For his own part, Blair has pitched himself as a candidate looking to push back on President Donald Trump’s cuts to areas like the Department of Education.

"You can’t fix a system that’s being dismantled from the top. Right now, Donald Trump is getting rid of the Department of Education and cutting money from schools that already have the least. That doesn’t just hurt some office in Washington. It hurts the kid in the back of the classroom in this district," Blair said during a campaign visit.

On his website, Blair lists Medicare-for-all, increasing the minimum wage and raising teacher pay among his top priorities.

STATE OF PLAY: DEMS BATTLE FOR SHOT AT CRUCIAL ARIZONA HOUSE SEAT AMID GOP'S RAZOR-THIN MAJORITY

Although the winner will have secured the seat in the special election, they must still win a general election in November to fill the seat for a full term.

David Scott last won re-election in 2024 in a 71.8% to 28.2% victory over his Republican challenger Jonathan Chavez.

item.title: French man discovers 5 dead babies hidden in boxes in his home after argument with wife: prosecutors
item.description: A husband in France found five decomposing babies in cardboard boxes after arguing with his wife, who had given birth at home to a baby boy the day before.
item.content:encoded:
A man in France discovered remains believed to belong to five newborns hidden inside cardboard boxes in his home after his partner gave birth at home and was taken to a hospital, according to prosecutors.

He became distressed after he found out about her pregnancy at ⁠a very late stage, despite her repeated denials, and began searching their home, prosecutors said. The couple already had two children, ages eight and nine.

The woman, 32, who was not identified, was allegedly arguing with her husband over what was in the boxes at their home in the town of Orange on Monday after she gave birth at home to a baby boy the day before.

She started complaining about abdominal pain during the argument on Monday. She was taken to a hospital and her husband stayed behind and discovered the dead babies hidden in the boxes.

NEWBORN VANISHED AFTER SECRET BIRTH, PARENTS ALLEGEDLY CLAIMED BABY 'WAS A PRANK': COPS

The man, also 32, then notified authorities through the hospital ​where the woman was being treated for pain.

"The husband stayed behind when she was taken to the hospital, and looked inside the cardboard boxes they had been arguing over – that’s when he found the five dead babies," an investigating source said, according to the US Sun. "All the [fetuses] were decomposing, and had been around for quite a while."

Police searched the couple's home, and prosecutors opened a criminal investigation into suspected murder on Monday.

HEATED LINDSAY CLANCY COURTROOM EXCHANGE OVER 911 CALL, CRIME SCENE PHOTOS SETS STAGE FOR MOM’S MURDER TRIAL

A forensic pathologist estimated, based on initial findings, that the bones ​and decomposing remains belonged to five newborns.

Authorities said the remains included bones believed to belong to four newborns and the decomposing body of a fifth. Autopsies and further laboratory testing were ordered.

The man told ‌police ⁠he was unaware of his wife's possible pregnancies.

The public prosecutor's office urged child welfare services to assess the health of the couple's eight and nine-year old children. It ​also issued a ​provisional placement ⁠order for the newborn baby, pending referral of the case to a children's court judge.

The ​mother, who was still in the hospital on Tuesday, has not yet spoken to investigators.

A post-mortem examination has been ordered on ​the decomposing remains, and the bones will undergo anthropological analysis in a laboratory, according to prosecutors.

The couple had no history of problems and were described by a neighbor as "charming people," according to French outlet AFP.

The neighbor, Florent Jean, told the outlet that the wife was a stay-at-home mother and the husband worked. Jean said the two were "normal people, really."

Reuters contributed to this report.

item.title: Kentucky governor calls on McConnell to prove he is fit to serve or resign: 'Address the people'
item.description: Kentucky Gov. Andy Beshear demanded that Sen. Mitch McConnell prove his fitness to serve or resign after the 84-year-old's lengthy hospital stay.
item.content:encoded:
Kentucky Gov. Andy Beshear, a Democrat, is demanding that Sen. Mitch McConnell, R-Ky., prove he is fit to continue serving in Congress after a lengthy hospital stay or resign from office.

In a letter to McConnell, the governor urged the 84-year-old senator to directly address the people of Kentucky about his ability to serve.

"I am calling on you to directly and verbally address the people of Kentucky and provide proof of your capacity to serve, or resign," Beshear wrote to McConnell.

MCCONNELL OUT OF HOSPITAL, STILL NOT 'MEDICALLY CLEARED' TO RETURN TO SENATE

Beshear made the demand after McConnell’s office announced on Monday that he had been discharged from the hospital but had not yet been medically cleared to leave the rehabilitation facility where he has been undergoing physical therapy and return to office.

The senator's office said he would miss a major Kentucky political event and upcoming Senate votes.

"I'm still working hard to get back to my full schedule of work in the Senate and in Kentucky, keeping up with intense physical therapy per my doctors’ orders. Unfortunately, that means I won’t be able to make it to Fancy Farm, Kentucky, this Saturday ... As always, I appreciate all of your continued well wishes, and I’m looking forward to getting back to the Senate and to Kentucky soon," McConnell said in a statement.

McConnell was hospitalized on June 14 and later revealed that it was due to a fall at his home.

'THIS IS NOT NORMAL': AOC UNLOADS ON MCCONNELL'S PROLONGED ABSENCE

"Since his discharge from hospital care, he has maintained a strenuous course of physical therapy and rehabilitation, including multiple sessions a day designed to rebuild strength and reduce the risk of future falls. His bout with childhood polio continues to be a significant factor in his mobility. He is not yet medically cleared to leave the rehab facility and return to the office," the Attending Physician's office said in a statement.

The physician’s statement focused on McConnell’s mobility, physical rehabilitation and risk of future falls and did not raise concerns about his cognitive condition.

Beshear first urged McConnell earlier this month to release more information about his health after weeks of no public comments.

The governor also sent a letter on Tuesday to Senate Majority Leader John Thune, R-S.D., calling on him to investigate McConnell’s condition if the senator does not prove that he is capable of continuing his term.

"All of this speculation and even this letter could have been avoided with a minimal amount of transparency," Beshear wrote to Thune.

Fox News Digital has reached out to the offices of Beshear, McConnell and Thune.

Since he was hospitalized last month, McConnell's office has issued major updates on July 12 and July 27, with each notice featuring a photograph.

This comes amid intensified public scrutiny of aging elected officials in recent years over mental gaffes and deaths in office.

item.title: Caitlin Clark erupts for 32 points as Fever hold off Storm to complete season-series sweep
item.description: Caitlin Clark scored 32 points as the Indiana Fever beat the Seattle Storm 103-95, extending the Storm's home struggles at Climate Pledge Arena.
item.content:encoded:
The Seattle Storm had struggled at home entering Tuesday night, carrying a 4-10 record at Climate Pledge Arena into their third matchup of the season with the visiting Indiana Fever.

The Storm’s home-court woes continued Tuesday night as the Fever earned a 103-95 road win behind Caitlin Clark’s team-high 32 points. Natisha Hiedeman led all scorers with 33 for Seattle.

The Fever's West Coast trip continues Friday with a meeting against the Portland Fire.

Prosecutors appeared to begin chipping away at the defense’s portrayal of Lindsay Clancy as overmedicated, walking jurors through nine prescription bottles that still contained many of the pills she had been given.

Patrick Clancy testified Monday that his ex-wife had been prescribed numerous psychiatric medications in the months before the deaths of their three young children. But under questioning from Assistant District Attorney Shanan Buckingham, he acknowledged that several prescriptions had been only partly used.

"So there were a lot of pills prescribed, but not a lot of pills taken. Correct?" Buckingham asked, holding up a bag of prescription medications.

LINDSAY CLANCY’S EX-HUSBAND DETAILS ‘BIG SPIRAL’ AS EXPERT SAYS ONE PART ‘SCARED ME’ IN MOM’S MURDER TRIAL

Buckingham also sought to distinguish between the total number of medications prescribed over several months and how many Lindsay was prescribed at one time.

Patrick estimated that she was taking three or four medications at most. Buckingham then asked whether it would surprise him to learn that Lindsay was prescribed no more than three medications at any given time and usually two.

LINDSAY CLANCY’S HUSBAND COULD TESTIFY FOR HER AT TRIAL OVER DEATHS OF THEIR THREE CHILDREN

"It wouldn’t be terribly surprising, no," Patrick said.

Former federal prosecutor Neama Rahmani said the questioning appeared designed to prevent the defense from controlling how jurors view the cocktail of medications that Lindsay Clancy was prescribed in the months before authorities say she strangled Cora, 5, Dawson, 3, and Callan, 8 months, inside the family’s Duxbury home in January 2023.
